Subject: Request: compact KMS/HSM proofset for SIG addendum

Hannah,

We are finalizing the SIG addendum and need a compact artifact bundle that shows Redwood's KMS/HSM posture for our internal reviewers. Specifically, can you provide:
- HSM attestation or vendor statement for the HSM cluster used for root key material (latest available)
- A compact rotation proof (CSV or log extract) showing rotations over the last 12 months for customer envelope keys (anonymized IDs are fine)
- A short note describing in-transit encryption controls between the application layer and KMS (TLS versions, mutual TLS usage if applicable)

We're on a tight deadline for our audit kickoff next week. If you can send an archive or point me to a shared folder, that'd be ideal.

Thanks,
Daniel Reyes

Hi Daniel — thanks for the clear list. We're able to provide a concise bundle that covers each of those bullets. Quick notes up front:
- We can share the HSM vendor attestation (pdf) and an export of rotation events with anonymized key IDs.
- Transit: Redwood uses TLS1.2+ by default for internal RPC and TLS1.3 for customer-facing endpoints; between compute and KMS we enforce mTLS with cert pinning on Dedicated/Private deployments.

Vivek and Laura — looping you in to pull the artifacts and redact/anonymize as needed. Vivek, can you assemble the CSV summary and attach the attestation PDF? Laura, can you confirm whether any additional redaction is necessary for Acme's SIG?

Daniel — we'll target end of day Wednesday PST for a compact bundle and a short README that explains provenance and redaction. If that's too late, tell us and we'll prioritize earlier.

Hi all — attaching the preliminary artifacts per Hannah's note. Attachments: 
- hsm-attestation-2026-12.pdf (vendor attestation from HSM provider; redaction: customer names removed)
- kms-rotation-log-2026.csv (anonymized key IDs; rotation timestamps, actor, reason code)
- transit-tls-config.txt (snippet of the transport config showing TLS versions and mTLS requirement)

Couple of clarifications for Acme:
- The rotation CSV includes envelope keys only; root-of-trust key material is rotated on a longer cadence and is described in the attestation.
- Rotation events are recorded by our internal key-manager service; the CSV shows last 12 months (2026-01 through 2026-12).
- For Dedicated and Private deployments we do require mutual TLS between compute nodes and the KMS; hosted API uses short-lived mTLS session tokens and TLS1.3 for customer-facing egress.

If you need a signed audit statement in addition to the attestation, we can request the vendor to countersign — that would add a day.

2) For the mTLS between compute and KMS in Dedicated, can you provide the expected certificate lifetime and rotation process for the node identity certs?
3) We're redacting nothing at the moment but may need minimal redaction for log actor IDs — will flag if/when.

If you can answer (1) and (2) in a short paragraph, that should satisfy our reviewers. Appreciate the quick turnaround.

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Request: compact KMS/HSM proofset for SIG addendum

Daniel — answers inline and a link to the folder with the compact bundle: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2bKMS-HandShake-Audit

1) Rotation policy (customer envelope keys): default rotation cadence is 90 days for ephemeral envelope keys used in hosted APIs; customers can opt for 180 days in Dedicated/Private. Rotation is automated for envelope keys by our Key Manager Service (KMS) with scheduled rotation jobs. Policy enforcement: rotations are driven by policy entries stored in the KMS config; any failed rotation triggers an alert and a retry flow and is visible in the rotation audit stream.

2) Node identity certs (Dedicated): certificate lifetime for node identity certs is 30 days. Certificates are issued by our internal CA (short-lived certs) and rotated automatically via a certificate provisioning daemon that uses mTLS bootstrap tokens. On rotation, old certs remain valid for a short overlap window (default 2 hours) to prevent transient failures. We also support customer-managed CAs for Private deployments if requested.

Attachments have been uploaded to the Drive folder above; the archive contains a README that maps each artifact to SIG/CAIQ questions. If you need the HSM vendor countersignature, let us know — we can request it and provide within 24–48 hours.

Regards,
Hannah Schmitt
